violated_contract: Work handed to a thread pool must have an owner that outlives it. A coordinator may not submit into the pool it is itself running on, and no submitted unit of work may be the responsibility of a process that exits without joining that pool. A scheduled job whose per-item budget is enforced by asyncio.wait_for owns only the call it wraps; anything that call spawns and does not await is outside every budget and dies with the container.
canonical_prevention: Run the spawned work inline in the caller, inside the same per-item budget that governs the rest of that item, and contain its faults explicitly so containment stays a decision rather than a side effect of the discarded Future. Pin the negative half of the wiring - that the work is not submitted to any pool - with a source check, since a behavioral test can only observe the path that does run.
